note: Per-EVIDENCE-BRANCH capability CONTRACT, enforced by scanner/tests/test_claim_discipline.py. fact_capable/clean_capable are SEPARATE claims describing what is TRUE TODAY. target_fact_capable/target_clean_capable are what the branch MUST become — this registry is a ladder, not a ceiling. Any gap between current and target REQUIRES `blocking_work`: the concrete engineering that closes it. A gap without blocking work fails the enforcement test, so a capability can never be quietly abandoned by downgrading the claim; the claim stays, and the system is built up to meet it. Downgrading a TARGET requires an explicit `target_downgrade_rationale` stating why the capability is not achievable at all. `evidence_surface` is a CLOSED type (response_headers | response_body | transport | tls_handshake | service_response | artifact | composite | live_capture) — rules key off the declared type, never off the branch name, so a future body-derived branch cannot escape them by being called something else. `implementation_refs` point at the code that realises the branch; the enforcement test checks the referenced file and symbol actually exist. `control_requirements` is the CLOSED-vocabulary list of standing capability controls (gates / VIGIL-owned captures / instrumentation / primary-artifact parses) a branch depends on to reach its declared capability — distinct from `preconditions`, which admission evaluates per observation; for a LEAD-only branch it names the MISSING controls that `blocking_work` closes. `oracle_version` names the OracleKind whose deterministic decision procedure adjudicates a FACT on this branch — the FACT certificate binds verify.oracle_version(kind) at mint so a verifier re-runs the SAME procedure — and is EMPTY for a LEAD-only branch, which no VIGIL oracle adjudicates yet (that is its blocking_work). The manifest validator (integration/vigil_integration/live/tool_manifest.py:validate_branch_registry) enforces both columns: fact_capable ⇒ a named oracle_version, LEAD-only ⇒ none.

branches.evidence: HTTP 3xx status + Location header host equals the injected canary host
branches.limitation: Header-derived: independent of body decoding. A 3xx without a Location is not a followed redirect.
branches.blocking_work: INSERTION COVERAGE — DONE for open_redirect: the live re-drive now probes the redirect value across five insertion surfaces — URL query value, URL path segment, Cookie value, urlencoded-body value and JSON-body value — synthesising the cookie/urlencoded/JSON carriers with the correct method + Content-Type (integration/vigil_integration/live/web_redrive.py:_redirect_templates). The OpenRedirectCheck predicate fires only on a real navigation to the UNIQUE canary HOST, so no benign-twin baseline is needed for soundness. RESIDUAL: a CLEAN over the synthesised cookie/body surfaces is bounded to the probed candidate redirect-parameter names (the URL’s own query names plus _REDIRECT_PARAM_NAMES), never a claim of absence under a parameter name not probed — the WebRedriveResult coverage statement names the examined surfaces so the bound is explicit.

branches.evidence: meta-refresh target host in the rendered body equals the canary host
branches.limitation: NOT CLEAN-capable: a non-firing cannot distinguish 'the document contains no redirect' from 'we could not read the document'. Body availability is established ONLY for a complete, single-member gzip/deflate/identity stream whose charset is deterministically known (a BOM, the transport Content-Type charset, or the RFC-8259 UTF-8 default for application/json) and which decodes strictly; an undeclared charset, brotli/zstd, concatenated members, and truncated reads are INCONCLUSIVE, not CLEAN. Suppressed entirely on a followed 3xx, whose body is never rendered.
branches.blocking_work: Body evidence must become CLEAN-capable AND readable for every body, not only deterministically-declared ones. This needs: (1) a spec-compliant HTML encoding-determination implementation — a vendored reference, NOT a regex; a hand-approximated <meta> prescan is rejected under Claim-Discipline rule 4, and the transport charset must outrank the in-document declaration per WHATWG; (2) vendored, version-pinned, bounded STREAMING brotli/zstd decoders whose versions are bound into oracle provenance, so adjudication is host-independent and offline-replayable (dynamic host module-probing was removed for this reason); (3) bounded concatenated-member decoding so a multi-member body is read rather than refused; (4) a truncation-free read for pages under the cap. Only then is a non-firing a channel-confirmed negative. INSERTION COVERAGE — DONE for open_redirect: the live re-drive now injects the canary across query, URL path, Cookie, urlencoded-body and JSON-body insertion points via synthesised carriers (integration/vigil_integration/live/web_redrive.py:_redirect_templates), so a redirect reachable only from a cookie/body/JSON parameter is examined and can mint a FACT on this branch instead of sitting unexamined. This surface expansion is INDEPENDENT of the body-decode / render_dom completeness work above, which is what still blocks a body-derived CLEAN.

branches.evidence: a JS location sink assigning the canary host, where the sink BEGINS in a region the lexer proved is executable code
branches.limitation: Sinks in comments, string/template literals and ambiguous `/`-spans are excluded structurally by js_lex. The regex-vs-division ambiguity JavaScript cannot settle without parsing is resolved AWAY from minting, so an ambiguous span yields no FACT. NOT CLEAN-capable: this lexes but does not EXECUTE, so a sink built at runtime (string concatenation, eval, a framework router) is invisible and a non-firing cannot assert absence.
branches.blocking_work: CLEAN requires proving no sink exists, which lexing cannot do: a redirect assembled at runtime never appears literally. Closing it needs the headless browser path (render_dom) to observe actual navigation, not source inspection. INSERTION COVERAGE — DONE for open_redirect: the live re-drive now injects the canary across query, URL path, Cookie, urlencoded-body and JSON-body insertion points via synthesised carriers (integration/vigil_integration/live/web_redrive.py:_redirect_templates), so a redirect reachable only from a cookie/body/JSON parameter is examined and can mint a FACT on this branch instead of sitting unexamined. This surface expansion is INDEPENDENT of the body-decode / render_dom completeness work above, which is what still blocks a body-derived CLEAN.

branches.limitation: NOT CLEAN-capable: a non-firing cannot distinguish 'the app emits no Host-derived URL' from 'we could not read the document'. Inert markup (comments, raw-text elements, template fragments) is excluded via the stdlib tokenizer; an inert-text echo is not an emission.

INSERTION COVERAGE: host-header injection is a REQUEST-LEVEL surface — the re-drive sets a hostile Host header on the request (HostHeaderCheck) rather than fuzzing a query/body parameter — so this branch does not depend on cookie/urlencoded/JSON parameter insertion; the open_redirect re-drive is what gained those carriers (integration/vigil_integration/live/web_redrive.py:_redirect_templates).

branches.evidence: VIGIL's own minimal introspection query returns a well-formed schema (data.__schema.types is a non-empty array)
branches.limitation: Body-derived (the schema is in the JSON response body): NOT CLEAN-capable — a non-firing cannot distinguish 'introspection is disabled' from 'the response body could not be decoded'. Fires ONLY on a well-formed GraphQL introspection response whose data.__schema.types is a non-empty array, produced by VIGIL's OWN introspection query — never a tool's say-so, never the mere presence of a /graphql path; a 400/403 or a GraphQL 'errors' (introspection disabled) response fails the predicate.
branches.blocking_work: CLEAN-capability needs the same decode-completeness guarantee as open_redirect.body_markup, to distinguish 'introspection disabled' from 'body unreadable'; until then a non-firing is INCONCLUSIVE, never CLEAN. The proposition itself (a returned schema) is DEFINITE, so no benign-twin baseline is needed for the FACT.

branches.evidence: VIGIL's own TLS handshake and the certificate the peer presented
branches.limitation: Scoped to what a modern client still negotiates; it does not enumerate every legacy suite the server might accept.

branches.evidence: a concrete pinned version parsed by VIGIL falls in a pinned advisory's affected range
branches.limitation: NOT CLEAN-capable: absence from a PINNED advisory snapshot is not absence of vulnerability, and non-pinned constraints are skipped rather than resolved.

branches.evidence: a kube-bench CIS control VIGIL parsed from the operator's --json export hard-FAILED AND its retained actual_value literally carries a dangerous flag (--anonymous-auth=true, --authorization-mode=AlwaysAllow, a non-zero --insecure-port/--read-only-port, a static auth file, etc.)
branches.limitation: NOT CLEAN-capable: a kube-bench export is a PARTIAL, point-in-time snapshot of one target's control-plane flags, so the absence of a firing control does not prove the cluster is hardened. Claims are bounded to the parsed ARTIFACT ('this export records control X FAILED with value Y'), never to the live cluster; a WARN or a FAIL whose value shows the SECURE flag stays a LEAD.
branches.blocking_work: CLEAN requires a completeness proof over the artifact: that the export enumerates the FULL CIS control set for the target's role (master/etcd/controlmanager/scheduler/node) and that every applicable control PASSED, so 'no control fired' becomes a bounded negative rather than an absence of data. That needs a control-coverage manifest (the expected control IDs per node role + kube-bench version) checked against the parsed export before any CLEAN may be asserted.

branches.evidence: a ClusterRoleBinding/RoleBinding VIGIL parsed from the operator's manifest binds an ANONYMOUS subject (system:anonymous / system:unauthenticated) to a dangerous BUILT-IN ClusterRole (cluster-admin / admin / edit), with roleRef.kind=ClusterRole in the rbac.authorization.k8s.io apiGroup
branches.limitation: NOT CLEAN-capable: a manifest export is a PARTIAL snapshot of the bindings the operator handed us, so the absence of an anonymous-privileged binding does not prove none exists cluster-wide. Claims are bounded to the parsed ARTIFACT, never to the live cluster. NEAR-ZERO-FP by faithful roleRef carry: a namespaced Role named 'edit'/'admin', an anonymous binding to a custom/non-dangerous role, or a binding with no anonymous subject does NOT fire.
branches.blocking_work: CLEAN requires a completeness proof that the manifest stream enumerates EVERY ClusterRoleBinding and RoleBinding in the cluster (a full RBAC export, not a hand-picked subset) AND that the dangerous-role set is exhaustive (transitive aggregation into cluster-admin via aggregationRule, and custom roles whose rules grant '*' verbs on '*' resources). Only then is 'no anonymous-privileged binding found' a bounded negative rather than an absence of data.

branches.evidence: an Istio/Linkerd manifest VIGIL parsed DECLARES a permissive CONFIGURATION the mesh_posture oracle re-derives over the manifest construct: a PERMISSIVE/DISABLE PeerAuthentication mTLS mode, an ALLOW AuthorizationPolicy whose rule admits every caller AS DECLARED, or an all-unauthenticated Linkerd default-inbound-policy. This is the DECLARED configuration, not proven effective runtime posture — policy precedence, namespace/workload selectors and more-specific policies can change the effective result, which this slice does not evaluate.
branches.limitation: Bounded to what the RETAINED mesh CONFIG declares — the claim is about the manifest artifact, never that the live mesh accepts plaintext. NOT CLEAN-capable: a non-firing manifest is a lead, not a clean bill of health, because a partial/incomplete config export (only some namespaces/resources) cannot prove the ABSENCE of a permissive policy elsewhere, and an absent mtls_mode inherits a parent this slice does not resolve. requestPrincipals ['*'] is JWT-gated (not allow-all) and does not fire.
branches.blocking_work: CLEAN requires a completeness proof over the mesh config: enumerate every namespace/workload in scope, resolve PeerAuthentication mTLS inheritance to an effective mode per workload, and record that the export is complete, so 'no permissive policy matched' becomes a bounded negative rather than an absence of data. Until then a non-fire stays INCONCLUSIVE.

branches.evidence: a GitHub-Actions workflow VIGIL parsed contains a dangerous construct the cicd_posture oracle re-derives: a third-party action pinned to a MUTABLE ref, a pull_request_target that checks out the untrusted PR head (pwn-request), or a run step interpolating an untrusted github.event.* expression (script-injection)
branches.limitation: Bounded to what the RETAINED workflow FILE declares — the claim is about the workflow artifact, never that the pipeline was exploited. NOT CLEAN-capable: a non-firing workflow is a lead, not clean, because a single workflow file cannot prove the ABSENCE of risk across the repo's other workflows / reusable-workflow callees / composite actions this slice does not follow. First-party (actions/github) and SHA-pinned actions, a plain pull_request base checkout, and a quoted-literal-only interpolation do not fire.
branches.blocking_work: CLEAN requires a completeness proof over the CI/CD surface: enumerate every workflow file plus the reusable-workflow and composite-action callees they reference, resolve each transitively, and record the enumeration is complete, so 'no dangerous construct matched' becomes a bounded negative rather than an absence of data. Until then a non-fire stays INCONCLUSIVE.

branches.evidence: a resource VIGIL parsed from the target's OWN IaC artifact (a Terraform plan-JSON / tfstate, or a processed CloudFormation template) declares an UNAMBIGUOUS insecure achieved state — encryption-at-rest explicitly disabled on a sensitive store, an explicit public flag, a LITERAL wildcard principal in a policy document, an ACL/AccessControl literally granting AllUsers, or a security-group ingress literally open to 0.0.0.0/0 — re-derived by the deterministic cloud_posture oracle
branches.limitation: Bounded to the REPRESENTED/RESOLVED state of the parsed artifact ('this tfstate/template declares X'), NEVER a claim about live infrastructure. NOT CLEAN-capable: an IaC export is a PARTIAL, represented state, so a non-firing cannot distinguish 'no insecure state declared' from 'the artifact does not represent the whole resource'. An ambiguous attribute is UNKNOWN, never a guessed insecure fact: block_public_access=false -> public=None (not True); a missing SSE block -> encrypted=None (not False); a CloudFormation intrinsic (Ref/Fn::*) principal -> the grant is dropped. A plan's DESIRED value is weaker than applied state.
branches.blocking_work: CLEAN requires a COMPLETENESS proof over the artifact: prove the parsed plan/state/template enumerates the resource's FULL achieved policy surface (all attached bucket-policy/ACL/public-access-block/SSE/security-group resources resolved and cross-linked to the resource), and that intrinsics/parameters are fully resolved, so 'no insecure state declared' becomes a bounded negative about the resource rather than an absence of data. Until then a non-firing over a partial export stays INCONCLUSIVE.

branches.evidence: a REAL IAM grant PATH re-derived over the policy graph built from the target's OWN IaC artifact lets an anonymous/over-privileged principal reach a resource — judged by the deterministic policy_path oracle over the retained graph
branches.limitation: Bounded to the policy graph the parsed artifact REPRESENTS, NEVER a claim about a live cloud account. NOT CLEAN-capable: an IaC export is a PARTIAL represented state, so the absence of a firing path proves nothing about grants the artifact does not represent. The graph is re-derived from the raw artifact (never laundered from a scanner's say-so); a wildcard principal expressed via a CloudFormation intrinsic is UNKNOWN and contributes no grant.
branches.blocking_work: CLEAN requires a completeness proof that the parsed artifact represents the resource's ENTIRE IAM grant surface (every policy/role/attachment/assume/member edge resolved, no intrinsic or cross-stack reference unresolved), so 'no anonymous grant path' becomes a bounded negative rather than an absence of policy data. Until then a non-firing over a partial graph stays INCONCLUSIVE.

branches.evidence: a resource in a VIGIL-OWNED, D5-scope-gated LIVE cloud capture carries an UNAMBIGUOUS insecure achieved state (encryption-at-rest explicitly disabled on a sensitive store, an explicit public flag, a LITERAL wildcard principal, an ACL granting AllUsers, or a security-group ingress open to 0.0.0.0/0) re-derived by the deterministic cloud_posture oracle over the RETAINED capture
branches.limitation: Bounded to the CAPTURED, SCOPED live state ('in provider/account[/region], resource R is insecure as captured at T'), NOT the whole cloud. NOT CLEAN-capable: the capture is a PARTIAL, scoped enumeration, so a non-firing cannot distinguish 'no insecure state' from 'not captured'. The D5 gate authorises the (provider, account[, region][, resource]) against the signed charter BEFORE any capture is adjudicated (fail-closed); the collector mints only a native-inventory LEAD, and the FACT rests on VIGIL's own oracle re-derivation, never the collector's say-so.
branches.blocking_work: CLEAN requires a COMPLETENESS proof over the capture: prove the scoped enumeration covered EVERY in-scope resource + its full achieved policy surface (all bucket-policy/ACL/public-access-block/SSE/security-group state resolved) and record the requested-vs-returned scope as complete, so 'no insecure state' becomes a bounded negative rather than an absence of data. Until then a non-firing over a partial capture stays INCONCLUSIVE.

branches.evidence: a resource in a VIGIL-OWNED, D5-scope-gated LIVE cloud capture grants a NAMED principal whose PARSED account is NOT in the charter's authorized owner-account set threaded into the retained control (owner_account / owner_accounts) — a cross-account trust re-derived by the deterministic cloud_posture oracle (rule named_cross_account_principal) over the RETAINED capture, never the collector's say-so. SOUNDLY attributable (FACT-capable) principals: an AWS account/role/user/STS ARN or bare 12-digit account (cross-ACCOUNT), and a GCP user/group/domain member (cross-DOMAIN). A GCP serviceAccount member is NOT FACT-capable here (it stays a LEAD) — see limitation.
branches.limitation: SOUND ONLY when the owner's own-account id(s) are threaded into the retained control from the charter: distinguishing an INTENDED same-account grant from a risky cross-account one REQUIRES the owner account. With NO owner-account set (unknown owner) the rule stays a LEAD — it NEVER guesses the owner and so never false-FACTs an intended internal grant. A principal whose account cannot be SOUNDLY parsed (a service ARN with an empty account field, a non-12-digit account, ANY GCP serviceAccount member, a bare non-prefixed FQDN principal such as an AWS service principal / OIDC issuer / IP, or an opaque canonical-user id) is un-attributable and never fires. GCP serviceAccount cross-PROJECT is deliberately NOT FACT-capable: a Google-MANAGED service agent (bigquery-encryption, dlp-api, gcp-sa-*, *-robot, etc. — granted CMEK/DLP/log-sink in ~every project) is indistinguishable by email from an external customer SA, and the Google-agent project set CANNOT be enumerated (Google adds agents), so any allow/deny list is fail-OPEN (a benign agent would fire a false FACT). Therefore every serviceAccount grant stays a LEAD. blocking_work: sound GCP-SA-cross-project needs an authoritative Google-service-agent registry OR an owner-supplied trusted-external-project allowlist threaded from the charter. (AWS cross-account: a grant to a benign AWS-service-owned account, e.g. a log-delivery account, is a real-but-low-risk cross-account grant that DOES fire — a documented precision nuance, not a false FACT.) Bounded to the CAPTURED, SCOPED live state at capture time, NOT the whole cloud. NOT CLEAN-capable: the capture is a PARTIAL, scoped enumeration, so a non-firing cannot distinguish 'no cross-account grant' from 'not captured' or 'owner unknown'.
branches.blocking_work: CLEAN requires (a) the live capture to THREAD the charter's authorized own-account id(s) into every retained control's owner_account/owner_accounts (so the comparison is grounded rather than absent), and (b) a COMPLETENESS proof over the capture: prove the scoped enumeration covered EVERY in-scope resource + its full principal/grant surface (every resource-policy/trust-policy/ACL statement resolved), so 'no cross-account grant' becomes a bounded negative rather than an absence of data. Until then a non-firing over a partial capture, or one with no owner-account threaded in, stays INCONCLUSIVE.

branches.evidence: a REAL IAM grant PATH re-derived over the policy graph built from a VIGIL-OWNED, D5-scope-gated LIVE cloud capture lets an anonymous/over-privileged principal reach a resource, judged by the deterministic policy_path oracle over the retained graph
branches.limitation: Bounded to the policy graph the SCOPED live capture represents, NOT the whole account. NOT CLEAN-capable: a partial scoped capture proves nothing about grants outside its scope. The D5 gate fails closed on an out-of-scope request; the graph is re-derived from the retained capture, never a scanner's say-so.
branches.blocking_work: CLEAN requires a completeness proof that the scoped capture enumerated the account's ENTIRE IAM grant surface in scope (every policy/role/attachment/assume/member edge), so 'no anonymous grant path' becomes a bounded negative. Until then a non-firing stays INCONCLUSIVE.

branches.evidence: a VIGIL-OWNED, WARDEN-A2- and D5-scope-gated capture from an instance-metadata endpoint retained BOTH a structurally-valid cloud credential (an AWS AccessKeyId+SecretAccessKey+Token from 169.254.169.254/iam/security-credentials, or a GCP Bearer access_token from computeMetadata/v1 service-accounts token) AND a confirming call (sts:GetCallerIdentity / a GCP tokeninfo) that authenticated with the SAME credential, bound by a shared credential fingerprint, all re-derived as an achieved-effect FACT by the deterministic imds_credential_capture oracle over the RETAINED, secret-safe capture
branches.limitation: Bounded to the CAPTURED credential and its ONE confirming call ('a credential retrieved from the instance-metadata endpoint authenticated as identity I at time T'), NOT a claim about every instance credential or the whole account. NOT CLEAN-capable: a non-firing over one capture cannot distinguish 'no capturable credential' from 'not captured'. The retained capture is SECRET-SAFE — the credential's secret material is redacted to a presence marker — so the FACT re-verifies offline with no live secret; the confirming call is the WARDEN-gated runner's RETAINED evidence re-derived by VIGIL's own oracle, never the runner's say-so. Real-transport LIVE-FIRE (the runner against a real metadata endpoint) is deferred on an operator-provisioned lab credential; the runner and this admission / certificate / world-model wiring are complete and fixture-proven offline.
branches.target_downgrade_rationale: This branch is an ACHIEVED-EFFECT exploitation confirmation over a single scoped capture; proving the ABSENCE of a capturable metadata credential is a different capability (an IMDS/metadata POSTURE check that would enumerate the instance's metadata configuration for completeness), not this exploitation branch's target, so clean-capability is deliberately not pursued here.

branches.evidence: a VIGIL-OWNED, WARDEN-gated capture proved an EXPOSED secret (a structurally-recognized leaked credential — one of the closed recognizer set: an AWS AccessKeyId, a GitHub PAT prefix, a GitLab PAT prefix, a Slack token prefix) is VALID: a confirming call (sts:GetCallerIdentity / GitHub GET /user / GitLab GET /api/v4/user / Slack auth.test) authenticated with the secret, bound by a shared credential fingerprint over a trusted, per-TYPE-allow-listed transport, all re-derived as an achieved-effect FACT by the deterministic secret_credential_validity oracle over the RETAINED, secret-safe capture
branches.limitation: Bounded to the CAPTURED secret and its ONE confirming call ('this exposed credential authenticated as identity I at time T'), NOT a claim about every secret or the whole account. NOT CLEAN-capable: one confirming call cannot prove no capturable / valid secret exists. The retained capture is SECRET-SAFE — the secret VALUE is redacted to a presence marker — so the FACT re-verifies offline with no live secret. The source-semantics are INVERTED vs the IMDS branch: the exposure source (a JS literal, a git blob, a config path, an ARN) is retained as evidence but is NOT a firing gate; the ANTI-LAUNDERING gate is the per-TYPE confirming-endpoint allow-list, so an attacker-controlled 'confirming' endpoint cannot mint a FACT.
